name: Private S3 bucket policy granting one named in-account user - NOT public, NOT cross-account
note: IAM-1207 (private-bucket negative control, suite-2 test 32 shape). An S3 bucket policy grants s3:GetObject to a single named IAM user in the bucket owner's account (supplied explicitly, since S3 ARNs carry no account). A named principal is not anonymous, so PUBLIC-ACCESS must NOT fire; the owner account matches, so it is a direct same-account grant, not cross-account.
rationale: A bucket policy that names one specific IAM user principal is a private, scoped grant - it is not the wildcard '*' public-access shape, so PUBLIC-ACCESS must never fire (AWS only treats a resource policy as public when access is granted to '*'/{AWS:'*'} or is otherwise not restricted to fixed principal/source values). S3 bucket and object ARNs carry no account id, so the owning account is supplied explicitly in the context; it equals the principal's account, making this a direct same-account grant (RESOURCE-SAME-ACCOUNT-GRANT, medium), not cross-account. The resource is object-scoped ('.../*') and the action is an object action (s3:GetObject), so there is no action/resource-type mismatch. The user's identity policies still govern effective access; an applicable explicit Deny still blocks. Ref: docs/resource-policy-semantics.md sec 2.1 / 5 / 7.2.
